{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence is stronger in B. It cites three separate sourced Reddit posts from different segments: a structural engineer, an HR practitioner, and a therapist. A has only one sourced quote, because its second quote's URL was not retrieved and so counts as missing.",
    "B's price anchors are more verifiable. NeverFined ($29/$59/$99 per month), ExpirationOps ($49/mo or $490/yr) and ClearBot ($500–$800 per location per year) all have published prices with URLs. In A, four of seven competitors (CostSnap, QuotrPro, Roooster, Setell) have unpublished pricing, so the willingness-to-pay band rests mainly on EstimationPro, Outdoor Estimates and QuoteIQ.",
    "B's acquisition evidence is more specific to the category. It cites sourced CPCs of $10–13 for 'compliance software' and identifies SEO/content as the channel competitors have converged on, at a quoted $200–800 per post. A cites a generic $237 blended B2B SaaS CPL and a $0.01–$10+ CPC range, which is too wide to inform a budget.",
    "B's MVP has a narrower failure surface for a solo builder on a 90-day horizon. A tracking-only tool with alerts and disclaimers already uses the liability posture its competitors use. A's own brief flags two risks: estimate accuracy could cause financial harm to customers, and crew scheduling is likely not functional within six weeks.",
    "Both briefs show crowded markets with no clear wedge, so competition does not separate them. The difference comes from evidence quality and execution risk, and both favor B."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence rests on a single sourced Reddit quote ('1-2 hours per night writing quotes'). The second quote's URL was not retrieved and must be treated as missing. A's claim that EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates were built and run by single contractor-founders also has no cited source, which weakens the solo-feasibility argument in its case for.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both ideas enter crowded markets of about seven competitors, and neither brief identifies a defensible wedge. B wins mainly on volume and specificity of sourced evidence, not on any strong evidence of an unmet gap. B also has unsourced elements: the RegTech $14.50 CPC benchmark has no URL, and Mosey's price comes secondhand from a competitor's comparison table. Neither brief has conversion or churn data, so the 90-day paying-customer outcome is uncertain for both."
}
